name: dhcp
description: Module 23: DHCP — DORA on the wire, renew and release, pool exhaustion, no server, a rogue server and a bridge filter that stops it, and a relay
setup:
cat > ${EVIDENCE}/dhcp-decode <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# one line per DHCP message in a capture: time, type, source → destination and the fields that matter
tshark -r "$1" -Y dhcp -T fields -E separator='|' -e frame.time_relative -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e dhcp.option.dhcp \
  -e dhcp.ip.your -e dhcp.ip.relay -e dhcp.option.router -e dhcp.option.ip_address_lease_time -e dhcp.flags.bc \
  -e dhcp.option.requested_ip_address -e dhcp.ip.client 2>/dev/null |
awk -F'|' '{split("DISCOVER OFFER REQUEST DECLINE ACK NAK RELEASE INFORM",T," ");
  printf "%7.3fs  %-8s %s → %s", $1, T[$4], $2, $3
  if ($11!="" && $11!="0.0.0.0") printf "  ciaddr %s", $11
  if ($5!="" && $5!="0.0.0.0") printf "  yiaddr %s", $5
  if ($6!="" && $6!="0.0.0.0") printf "  giaddr %s", $6
  if ($10!="") printf "  requested %s", $10
  if ($7!="") printf "  router %s", $7
  if ($8!="") printf "  lease %ss", $8
  if ($9=="1" || $9=="True") printf "  [broadcast flag]"
  print ""}'
EOF
chmod 755 ${EVIDENCE}/dhcp-decode
teardown: for p in ${EVIDENCE}/*.pid; do [ -f "$p" ] && kill $(cat "$p") 2>/dev/null; done; true

nodes.name: relay
setup: ethtool -K eth0 tx off >/dev/null; ethtool -K eth1 tx off >/dev/null

checks.name: DORA: c1 broadcasts DISCOVER from 0.0.0.0; the server OFFERs an address (unicast to the offered address — no broadcast flag set), c1 REQUESTs it by broadcast so every server hears the choice, the server ACKs; the address, default route and lease file follow
run: ip netns exec nl-dhcp-c1 tcpdump -i eth0 -n --immediate-mode -U -w ${EVIDENCE}/dora.pcap 'udp port 67 or udp port 68' 2>/dev/null & T=$!; sleep 1; ip netns exec nl-dhcp-c1 setsid busybox udhcpc -f -i eth0 -s ${EVIDENCE}/udhcpc.script -p ${EVIDENCE}/c1.pid -t 4 -T 4 > ${EVIDENCE}/c1-udhcpc.log 2>&1 & for i in $(seq 50); do grep -q 'udhcpc bound' ${EVIDENCE}/c1-udhcpc.log && break; sleep 0.2; done; sleep 0.5; kill -INT $T; wait $T 2>/dev/null; echo '--- on the wire:'; ${EVIDENCE}/dhcp-decode ${EVIDENCE}/dora.pcap; echo '--- c1:'; grep -E 'bound|lease of' ${EVIDENCE}/c1-udhcpc.log; echo "c1: $(ip netns exec nl-dhcp-c1 ip -4 -br addr show eth0 | awk '{print $3}') default $(ip netns exec nl-dhcp-c1 ip route show default | awk '{print $3}')"; echo '--- server lease file:'; cat ${EVIDENCE}/server.leases

checks.name: renewal (what happens at T1 = half the lease; SIGUSR1 makes udhcpc do it now): one unicast REQUEST to the server that granted the lease, one unicast ACK — no DISCOVER, no broadcast
run: ip netns exec nl-dhcp-c1 tcpdump -i eth0 -n --immediate-mode -U -w ${EVIDENCE}/renew.pcap 'udp port 67 or udp port 68' 2>/dev/null & T=$!; sleep 1; kill -USR1 $(cat ${EVIDENCE}/c1.pid); sleep 2; sleep 0.5; kill -INT $T; wait $T 2>/dev/null; echo '--- on the wire:'; ${EVIDENCE}/dhcp-decode ${EVIDENCE}/renew.pcap; grep -c renew ${EVIDENCE}/c1-udhcpc.log | sed 's/^/renew events logged by udhcpc: /'

checks.name: release (SIGUSR2): c1 sends RELEASE and drops the address; the server deletes the lease at once instead of waiting for it to expire
run: ip netns exec nl-dhcp-server tcpdump -i eth0 -n --immediate-mode -U -w ${EVIDENCE}/release.pcap 'udp port 67 or udp port 68' 2>/dev/null & T=$!; sleep 1; kill -USR2 $(cat ${EVIDENCE}/c1.pid); sleep 1; sleep 0.5; kill -INT $T; wait $T 2>/dev/null; echo '--- on the wire:'; ${EVIDENCE}/dhcp-decode ${EVIDENCE}/release.pcap; echo "c1: $(ip netns exec nl-dhcp-c1 ip -4 -br addr show eth0 | awk '{print $3}') default $(ip netns exec nl-dhcp-c1 ip route show default | awk '{print $3}')"; echo "server lease file: $(wc -l < ${EVIDENCE}/server.leases) lease(s)"; kill $(cat ${EVIDENCE}/c1.pid); rm -f ${EVIDENCE}/c1.pid

checks.name: pool exhaustion: the range holds two addresses; c1 and c2 take them, c3's DISCOVERs get no OFFER at all — the server logs 'no address available', the client just sees silence
run: ip netns exec nl-dhcp-server tcpdump -i eth0 -n --immediate-mode -U -w ${EVIDENCE}/exhausted.pcap 'udp port 67 or udp port 68' 2>/dev/null & T=$!; sleep 1; ip netns exec nl-dhcp-c1 setsid busybox udhcpc -f -i eth0 -s ${EVIDENCE}/udhcpc.script -p ${EVIDENCE}/c1.pid -t 4 -T 4 > ${EVIDENCE}/c1-udhcpc.log 2>&1 & for i in $(seq 50); do grep -q 'udhcpc bound' ${EVIDENCE}/c1-udhcpc.log && break; sleep 0.2; done; ip netns exec nl-dhcp-c2 setsid busybox udhcpc -f -i eth0 -s ${EVIDENCE}/udhcpc.script -p ${EVIDENCE}/c2.pid -t 4 -T 4 > ${EVIDENCE}/c2-udhcpc.log 2>&1 & for i in $(seq 50); do grep -q 'udhcpc bound' ${EVIDENCE}/c2-udhcpc.log && break; sleep 0.2; done; grep -h 'udhcpc bound' ${EVIDENCE}/c1-udhcpc.log ${EVIDENCE}/c2-udhcpc.log; ip netns exec nl-dhcp-c3 busybox udhcpc -i eth0 -s ${EVIDENCE}/udhcpc.script -n -q -t 3 -T 2 2>&1 | grep -E 'udhcpc (bound|leasefail|nak)|lease of|no lease'; sleep 0.5; kill -INT $T; wait $T 2>/dev/null; echo '--- on the wire:'; ${EVIDENCE}/dhcp-decode ${EVIDENCE}/exhausted.pcap; echo '--- server log:'; grep -o 'DHCPDISCOVER.*no address available' ${EVIDENCE}/server.log | sort | uniq -c

checks.name: free the pool: c1 and c2 release (SIGUSR2) and the server drops both leases at once; c3 then gets an address
run: kill -USR2 $(cat ${EVIDENCE}/c1.pid); sleep 0.3; kill $(cat ${EVIDENCE}/c1.pid); rm -f ${EVIDENCE}/c1.pid; kill -USR2 $(cat ${EVIDENCE}/c2.pid); sleep 0.3; kill $(cat ${EVIDENCE}/c2.pid); rm -f ${EVIDENCE}/c2.pid; sleep 0.3; echo "lease file: $(wc -l < ${EVIDENCE}/server.leases) lease(s)"; ip netns exec nl-dhcp-c3 busybox udhcpc -i eth0 -s ${EVIDENCE}/udhcpc.script -n -q -t 4 -T 4 2>&1 | grep -E 'udhcpc (bound|leasefail|nak)|lease of|no lease'

checks.name: no server: with the server's switch port down, c1 retries DISCOVER and gives up — on Linux nothing assigns 169.254.x.x unless a link-local helper (avahi-autoipd, NetworkManager ipv4.link-local) is configured
run: ip netns exec nl-dhcp-switch ip link set p1 down; ip netns exec nl-dhcp-c1 tcpdump -i eth0 -n --immediate-mode -U -w ${EVIDENCE}/noserver.pcap 'udp port 67 or udp port 68' 2>/dev/null & T=$!; sleep 1; ip netns exec nl-dhcp-c1 busybox udhcpc -i eth0 -s ${EVIDENCE}/udhcpc.script -n -q -t 4 -T 1 2>&1 | grep -E 'udhcpc (bound|leasefail|nak)|lease of|no lease'; sleep 0.5; kill -INT $T; wait $T 2>/dev/null; echo '--- on the wire:'; ${EVIDENCE}/dhcp-decode ${EVIDENCE}/noserver.pcap; ip netns exec nl-dhcp-switch ip link set p1 up; echo "c1: $(ip netns exec nl-dhcp-c1 ip -4 -br addr show eth0 | awk '{print $3}') default $(ip netns exec nl-dhcp-c1 ip route show default | awk '{print $3}')"

checks.name: rogue DHCP server: a second dnsmasq on the segment answers every DISCOVER too; the client takes the first OFFER, and a rogue that skips dnsmasq's ping-before-offer answers first — the clients end up with the attacker as gateway and DNS
run: ip netns exec nl-dhcp-rogue dnsmasq --conf-file=/dev/null --port=0 --user=root --log-dhcp --no-ping --interface=eth0 --bind-interfaces --dhcp-range=198.18.230.150,198.18.230.160,255.255.255.0,2m --dhcp-option=option:router,198.18.230.66 --dhcp-option=option:dns-server,198.18.230.66 --dhcp-leasefile=${EVIDENCE}/rogue.leases --log-facility=${EVIDENCE}/rogue.log --pid-file=${EVIDENCE}/rogue.pid; sleep 1; for n in c3 c2 c3 c2; do echo "--- $n:"; ip netns exec nl-dhcp-$n tcpdump -i eth0 -n --immediate-mode -U -w ${EVIDENCE}/rogue-$n.pcap 'udp port 67 or udp port 68' 2>/dev/null & T=$!; sleep 1; ip netns exec nl-dhcp-$n busybox udhcpc -i eth0 -s ${EVIDENCE}/udhcpc.script -n -q -t 4 -T 4 2>&1 | grep -E 'udhcpc bound'; sleep 0.5; kill -INT $T; wait $T 2>/dev/null; echo '--- on the wire:'; ${EVIDENCE}/dhcp-decode ${EVIDENCE}/rogue-$n.pcap | grep -E 'udhcpc bound|OFFER'; done

checks.name: DHCP snooping, by hand: a bridge rule drops server→client DHCP (UDP source port 67) arriving from any port but the server's; the rogue's OFFERs die at the switch and c3 gets only the real server's
relay: 'remote' is on another subnet; the relay turns its broadcast into a unicast to the server with giaddr = its own interface on that subnet, and the server picks the range (and router) by giaddr
run: ip netns exec nl-dhcp-relay tcpdump -i eth0 -n --immediate-mode -U -w ${EVIDENCE}/relay.pcap 'udp port 67 or udp port 68' 2>/dev/null & T=$!; sleep 1; ip netns exec nl-dhcp-remote busybox udhcpc -i eth0 -s ${EVIDENCE}/udhcpc.script -n -q -t 4 -T 4 2>&1 | grep -E 'udhcpc (bound|leasefail|nak)|lease of|no lease'; sleep 0.5; kill -INT $T; wait $T 2>/dev/null; echo '--- on the wire:'; ${EVIDENCE}/dhcp-decode ${EVIDENCE}/relay.pcap; echo "remote: $(ip netns exec nl-dhcp-remote ip -4 -br addr show eth0 | awk '{print $3}') default $(ip netns exec nl-dhcp-remote ip route show default | awk '{print $3}')"
